catalyst_notes: The macro catalyst environment for a non-Chinese antimony development asset has been exceptionally strong since September 2024 when China imposed formal export controls on antimony — restricting supply from a country that controls an estimated 70–80% of global primary antimony production. These controls catalysed urgent government interest from Canada, the United States, the EU, and Australia in domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains, with antimony explicitly named across multiple critical minerals frameworks. The Foxtrot project, as a past-producing Canadian antimony asset in a Tier-1 jurisdiction, is well-positioned to attract federal (NRCan) and provincial (Newfoundland) grant interest under Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy and related programs. Company-specific near-term catalysts — drill programs, resource updates, government grants announced, offtake discussions, strategic partnerships — cannot be identified due to IR site inaccessibility. Score of 3 reflects the strong and durable macro tailwind offset by inability to identify company-level execution milestones.

analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (CRI.V) holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine in central Newfoundland — one of the few Western antimony development assets with a historical production record and Tier-1 jurisdiction credentials. The investment thesis rests heavily on the macro: China's September 2024 antimony export controls effectively restricted supply from the dominant global producer and have driven sustained strategic interest from Western governments in non-Chinese antimony supply chains. Foxtrot is well-positioned to attract government grant support and strategic partnership interest under this framework. The fundamental constraint on conviction is data availability: the company IR site has returned 403 errors on all automated fetch attempts across multiple consecutive runs; the most recent NI 43-101 technical report (August 2023) yielded no compliant resource estimate in the pre-extracted filing; and share-instrument details (strike prices, expiry dates) remain incomplete. The 316.7 million basic share count is structurally heavy for a pre-resource junior, and the 23.45 million option pool adds dilution uncertainty. Cap-table data sourced from April 2026 MD&A (extracted May 2026) — most recent available. Maintain WATCH at low confidence: the strategic optionality on a critical mineral in a Tier-1 jurisdiction justifies continued monitoring, but the absence of a defined resource and the persistent data opacity prevent a higher conviction score.
